  SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  MAY 9, 2016

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A special meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
  called to order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
  North, by CHAIR SCHACHTER.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR SCHACHTER led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Zigrang, Yoo, Conway, Thomas, Scott, Chair
  Schachter
  Commissioners Absent:  None
  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER SCOT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER CONWAY,

  TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING OF FEBRUARY 29, 2016.

  AYES:  Medawar, Zigrang, Yoo, Conway, Thomas, Scott, Chair Schachter
  NOES:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None.

  None.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 25-14; APPLICANT: MS. JUDY CHAI;
  LOCATION: 5883 CREST ROAD; A REQUEST FOR A GRADING
  APPLICATION, ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT, TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP,
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT, GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT, ZONE
  CHANGE, AND A NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY DETERMINATION FOR
  THE CONSTRUCTION OF FOUR SINGLE-FAMILY PATIO HOMES ON A .51-
  ACRE PARCEL. APPROVAL OF A MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION
  HAS ALSO BEEN PREPARED UNDER THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT (CEQA). MODIFICATIONS TO THE PLANS AS PREVIOUSLY
  REVIEWED BY THE CITY COUNCIL ON AUGUST 11, 2015, ARE PROPOSED.

Planning Commission Minutes  1
May 9, 2016
   THE STAKING AND FLAGGING HAVE BEEN REVISED TO DEMONSTRATE
  THE REDUCTIONS IN SCALE OF THE PROJECT.

  Associate Planner Thom gave a brief Staff Report, per the written material.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked about additional parking spaces within the zoning
  allowances, and Associate Planner Thom confirmed that they are permitted.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked how there could be no Variances when this application
  doesn’t come close to meeting RPD zoning requirements. Planning Director Wahba
  provided a history of the lot and the possible options available, pointing out that it is a
  difficult lot and an anomaly in the city. It doesn’t work as a commercial lot and is
  surrounded by residential development. The lot does comply with RPD zoning lot
  coverage requirements and will probably end up getting a Variance for the open
  space/recreational area component.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY pointed out that the direction from City Council and Staff
  discusses three freestanding patio homes and asked whether there are other single-
  family residential developments in the city at a density of 8 units per acre. Planning
  Director Wahba pointed out a development on Peppertree Lane that was approved in
  the late 1990s and one in Hillcrest Meadows. Both developments included CUPs and
  met the 10 acre requirement.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked about a single-family home, and Planning Director Wahba
  advised that the applicant is not interested in that option.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about privacy issues created by the one single-
  story home among the other two-story homes, and Planning Director Wahba explained
  that it is not optimal but is an option.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR,

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  At CHAIR SCHACHTER’S invitation, Judy Chai (applicant at 5883 West Crest Road)
  came forward and presented the application. Ms. Chai read a prepared speech
  providing a history of the property, her ownership of the property and the proposed
  redesigns. Ms. Chai pointed out that patio homes will enhance the property values of
  the neighbors and is preferred by them over selling the lot as a commercial property.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY asked about her resistance to reducing the number of units
  from four to three, and Ms. Chai responded with her economic concerns.
  COMMISSIONER CONWAY explained that the Commission considers land use and not
  economic aspects of the property

  Gary Maxwell (architect at 8941 Atlanta Avenue, Huntington Beach) came forward and
  explained the economic need for four units and the applicant’s goal to live in one of the
  units. Mr. Maxwell further explained that condominiums are passé and not as desirable
  as patio homes and that the property wouldn’t divide evenly into three lots because of
  the corner.

  Doug Maupin (developer at 27541 Palos Verdes drive East, Ranch Palos Verdes) came
  forward and discussed the property and the benefits of including it with the RPD property
  behind it. It would be a good addition to the corner, and requesting one less unit
  wouldn’t really improve the situation.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT,

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY asked about City Council and Staff’s direction for three
  units, and Planning Director Wahba explained that City Council had difficulty with the
  application, so there was discussion around making the units smaller and reducing the
  project to three units. There was also discussion relative to an attached single building
  with 3-4 units. This proposal is probably the best attempt possible with a four-unit
  development. The approach of fewer units going bigger isn’t necessarily the right

Planning Commission Minutes  2
May 9, 2016
   approach. Three units in the 2,000 square foot ballpark would probably meet the 70
  percent open space requirement.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY asked about merging the property with the adjoining RPD
  property to eliminate the 10 acre limitation, and Planning Director Wahba explained that
  a lot merger would be a difficult, process with the homeowners association and CC&Rs
  at Seaview.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked whether it is mathematically possible to get four units on
  the property with RPD zoning, and Planning Director Wahba responded that what
  doesn’t work is the 70 percent open area requirement. The best solution would look like
  a single three-unit building, but that would probably not be economically feasible.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR commented that this is an unpractical lot, and four big
  homes on that property doesn’t calculate.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT discussed the previous designs and commented that this
  redesign is a huge improvement, but the only truly viable approach is the RPD zone.
  There will never be a successful commercial development on the property. RA-20 or
  RA-10 zoning doesn’t work. A Variance would be supportable due to the unique
  limitations of this property, but this design maximizes the amount of driveway,
  commitment to parking and impacts. It gives more mass than one building with three or
  four units, which would exactly match compatibility with the Seaview homes. The
  dominant feature of that corner is attached units. City Council and this Commission was
  very clear that a one building or three-unit solution needed to be considered.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG advised that he had history with this project about 10 years
  ago but has no interest in the project and can look at it with an open mind and then
  commented that the way it is right now is too tight right on the corner. Building three
  units might be better than selling it as commercial property.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY suggested that the applicant present three patio homes
  around 2,000 square feet each, achieving close to the 70 percent open space
  requirement, or come forward with four townhomes in one building, no more than 2,000
  square feet each that achieves eight density units per acre with no Variances.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER agreed that submitting plan A and plan B would be efficient and
  again pointed out that the Commission cannot consider economic factors.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR,

  TO RE-OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  At CHAIR SCHACHTER’S invitation, Mr. Maupin re-approached and discussed a similar
  project in Rancho Palos Verdes with an RA-10 type of zone and two larger units.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT pointed out that two units at 3,000 square feet doesn’t need
  to be an RA-10 zone.

  Ms. Chai re-approached and pointed out that the patio home concept is clearly preferred
  by the Seaview homeowners association, which doesn’t want to see one large building,
  whether it be a townhome or commercial building.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER discussed the trees blocking the view of these homes from
  Seaview, and COMMISSIONER YOO asked whether it’s plausible to create a four-unit
  pad and comply with the 70 percent open space requirement.

  Mr. Maxwell re-approached and advised that rough calculations show that it would be a
  struggle to make it work and can’t work if guest parking spaces are counted against that.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO,

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT agreed that there is no way to get more than three patio
  homes and maybe four units in a single building and commented that he would consider
  two larger units.

Planning Commission Minutes  3
May 9, 2016
   COMMISSIONER CONWAY suggested that avoiding an RPD zone would avoid a
  Variance because it would go straight to an RA-10 zone. Planning Director Wahba
  added that it would need to be under 3,000 square foot livable area with a two-car
  garage.

  COMMISSIONER YOO commented that he prefers that the applicant do his own
  calculations with guidance, and Planning Director Wahba clarified that moving to three
  units from four would probably still fail if the three units were increased in size and
  recommended three homes not to exceed 6,000 square feet of livable area.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR,

  TO RE-OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  At CHAIR SCHACHTER’S invitation, Mr. Maxwell re-approached and discussed possible
  design solution details with Planning Director Wahba.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked about two duplexes, and Planning Director Wahba was
  hesitant about that option working aesthetically.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR,

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  The Commission and Staff clarified that a two building option would also need to stay
  within 6,000 square feet, and four freestanding units are not an option. It was also
  clarified that the applicant would not need to re-flag the project.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT,

  TO RE-OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER CONWAY moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO,

  TO CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 25-14 TO THE JUNE 6, 2016
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING TO ALLOW APPLICANT TO WORK WITH
  STAFF ON THE THREE DIFFERENT OPTIONS OUTLINED.

  AYES:  Medawar, Zigrang, Yoo, Conway, Thomas, Scott, Chair Schachter
  NOES:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
  ABSENT:  None.

  Planning Director Wahba explained that there would be no new public notification.

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT and about an obtrusive Country Club sign at the corner of
  Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East. Planning Director Wahba
  advised that staff is looking into it.

10.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS

  Planning Director Wahba advised the Commission of the new Granicus digital agenda
  management system that will be put into place.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS (03 22 16)

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS (04 12 16)

Planning Commission Minutes  4
May 9, 2016
   C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS (04 26 16)

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A THROUGH 11C.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

13.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 9:04 p.m. CHAIR SCHACHTER adjourned the Planning Commission meeting to the
  regular meeting of June 6, 2016, at 7:00 p.m.
